subject: Control plane power sequencing, network policy and PVC fallback runbook — Warehouse Tech
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Harper <ben@warehousetech.com>, Alice Murray <alice@warehousetech.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Control plane power sequencing, network policy and PVC fallback runbook — Warehouse Tech

Hi Ben / Alice,

Per our intake call this morning, I wanted to put a short draft runbook for the on-site private cluster that covers three interdependent items we flagged: control-plane power sequencing (BMC and PDU behavior), network policy / VLAN constraints for tenant isolation, and a PVC fallback strategy for the NVMe-backed nodes in the single rack.

Summary of the ask:
- Control plane: define safe power sequence and recovery steps if the BMCs or PDUs reboot out-of-order. We need a minimal window (Target RTO: 7m) and a guaranteed quorum rejoin pattern.
- Network policy: because you only have two production VLANs and no upstream NAT for external egress, we need an ingress-only egress model (no outbound internet) plus strict L4 ACLs for the model-serving control plane and metrics collection.
- PVC fallback: ephemeral scratch on local NVMe + mirrored blockstore on a 2-node archive appliance. Plan for graceful evacuation if NVMe shows >85% write latency or SMART errors.

Attachments: site-inventory.csv (power outlets + BMC IPs), power-sequence.md (draft ordering and STONITH notes), rack-diagrams.png (top-of-rack and PDU mapping). I also dropped a folder with network diagrams to the Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExampleDiagram

Requesting:
1) Confirmation of PDU model and whether PDUs support sequenced turn-on via IP (we saw APC AP8851 listed but need confirmation).
2) Confirmation that BMC management network is physically separate and reachable from the control-plane subnet (no intermediate firewall).
3) Any constraints on outbound TLS to our telemetry endpoint (metrics.redwood.ai) — if blocked, we need a pull-proxy plan.

If this looks good I'll convert to a single-page runbook and propose on-site acceptance tests we can run during the 30-minute maintenance window.

Thanks,
Jordan
Principal Cloud Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Control plane power sequencing, network policy and PVC fallback runbook — Warehouse Tech

Jordan / Ben,

Thanks for the draft — quick notes after skimming the attachments. Quoting the key bits:

> Control plane: define safe power sequence and recovery steps if the BMCs or PDUs reboot out-of-order. We need a minimal window (Target RTO: 7m) and a guaranteed quorum rejoin pattern.

A few clarifying Qs:
- Are we planning an external etcd quorum (3 nodes) colocated in the same rack or split across two racks? The inventory looks like a single-rack footprint; if single rack we need a persistent witness (we usually recommend a tiny external witness VM or use a 3rd-party HA proxy).
- For STONITH behavior: the runbook should explicitly call out sequences to avoid split-brain when PDUs come back before BMCs are responsive. We should include a golden path and a fallback path (manual BMC cycle on node A then PDU cycle).

On the PVC fallback side:
- For workloads that tolerate brief restarts, prefer ReadWriteMany via the archive appliance for large model caches. If the appliance only exposes ReadWriteOnce, we'll need a syncing agent (rsync/replicator) and clear eviction policy on eviction.
- Suggest a node-exporter threshold alerting rule: node_disk_write_latency_seconds > 0.2 for 5m -> trigger automated cordon + drain to a pre-warmed burst pool. Include the Prometheus rule in the runbook.

Network policy:
- Given limited VLANs, we should use namespace-level NetworkPolicies + host-level egress ACLs on the Top-of-Rack switch. That combination gives tenant isolation without extra VLANs.
- We need to capture required ports for our sidecars (metrics, health probes, control-plane API) in a short allowlist.

I'll draft the STONITH matrix and the Prometheus rule after Ben confirms the PDU/BMC models.

Irene
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Adding a few concrete config-level suggestions so the ops team has something copy/paste-ready for the acceptance run:

Node pools / scheduling:
- Label plan: control-plane nodes => node-role.kubernetes.io/control=true; storage-nvme => storage=nvme; burst-worker => burst=true. Use podTopologySpreadConstraints for control-plane components across PDUs (if different PDUs exist).
- Taints: control-plane:NoSchedule on control-plane, and a toleration list for our system pods only.

PVC fallback pattern (implementation):
1) Primary: CSI driver -> local NVMe with Retain policy for immediate manual recovery.
2) Async replicate to archive appliance over iSCSI target with a small write-back buffer.
3) If local NVMe latency alarm fires (see Irene's threshold), automation will cordon+drain and scale up burst-worker pool (pre-warmed with model cache).

Sample Prometheus alert (for runbook):
ALERT NodeNVMeHighLatency
IF node_disk_write_latency_seconds{device=~"nvme.*"} > 0.2
FOR 5m
LABELS { severity = "critical" }
ANNOTATIONS { summary = "NVMe write latency high on {{ $labels.instance }}" }

NetworkPolicy snippets (K8s YAML) 
- default-deny-ingress and explicit allow for kube-apiserver IPs and metrics endpoints.

I can assemble the K8s snippets and a short Ansible play to perform the PDU/BMC health checks and run the acceptance test case (power-cycle one non-control node, ensure control-plane stays quorum).

-Karthik
Staff Software Engineer, Inference Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Control plane power sequencing, network policy and PVC fallback runbook — Warehouse Tech

Thanks — this is great detail. Quick confirmations from our side after talking to facilities and network: 

- PDU model is APC AP8851, chained to two PDUs per rack. PDUs support sequenced power-on via IP; we can provide a temporary admin account for the maintenance window.
- BMCs are on a separate management VLAN (VLAN 200), reachable from the control-plane subnet through a one-way ACL (control-plane can hit BMC SSH/Redfish, BMC cannot initiate sessions outbound).
- We cannot accept outbound HTTPS to external telemetry endpoints. All telemetry must be scraped/pulled by a local pull-proxy that we host in the management VLAN.
- Archive appliance is NetStore-2U with iSCSI targets exposing RWO; it can be mounted by two systems if we use an agent-based locker.

I've attached our network ACL spreadsheet (network-acls.xlsx) and updated the site inventory to mark PDU firmware versions.

Next steps from us: set up the temporary PDU admin account, provide a VPN push of the management VLAN for your engineers for Tuesday's test window, and confirm the pull-proxy endpoint location.

Ben
Head of Site Ops
Warehouse Tech

2) Produce the Prometheus alert rule and an Ansible health-check playbook for the PDU/BMC probes (cordon/drain test).
3) Draft the NetworkPolicy YAML (namespace-level) and a short host ACL checklist for your network team to apply (based on network-acls.xlsx).
4) Add a small section on cryptographic key handling: we will use an HSM-backed KMS for model keys; since outbound TLS is blocked, we'll configure KMS access over the management VLAN only.

Ben — please email the temporary PDU admin account to ops@redwood.ai and confirm the pull-proxy FQDN. I'll send the final runbook and snippets by Monday EOD so we have time to review before the maintenance window.

Thanks all,
